editorial.marketOverview: Friday's close remains the latest US cash market data. FT reports the Nasdaq 100 lost 5.6% Friday and 10.4% for the week, entering bear-market territory after a 20% retreat from October highs. Reuters reports Nasdaq Composite -5.28% and semiconductor index approximately -11%. Barron's reports VIX closed Friday at 37.66. All are historical Friday observations, not new Saturday trades.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with Saturday 02:27 EST snapshot, newly reviewed FT reporting explicitly confirms Nasdaq 100 bear-market territory and Barron's gives a more precise Friday VIX close of 37.66. Both quantify the same Friday selloff already incorporated in bearish bias. No fresh cash-market observation, new curated Open Watch event or three-day directional change is established.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Semiconductor and growth underperformance remains unusually severe, with broad risk aversion and heightened options protection demand. The new precise VIX figure reinforces rather than changes the existing volatility stress interpretation. Friday Reuters 10Y near 4.93% lacks a contemporaneous 2Y; older 4.94% and 4.65% imply +29 bp, but that stale spread is not a current yield curve. Fed rate-hike narratives are commentary without a verified direct CME probability. SEC probe media reports must not be conflated with verified enforcement findings or proven market causality.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23 faces downside continuation risk and potential oversold short-covering; US flash PMI at 09:45 ET can influence yields. Tuesday November 24 tests chip leadership through Analog Devices and Dell earnings and consumer confidence. Wednesday November 25 has concentrated GDP, PCE, jobless claims and other macro releases plus the Fed Beige Book ahead of Thanksgiving. High two-way volatility is plausible; no defensible numerical price targets without fresh matched quotes.
editorial.bullCase: Oversold Nasdaq 100 and high VIX create rebound potential, especially if yields ease and QQQ/SOX/SMH recover together with breadth and volatility confirmation. No durable reversal has yet been observed.
editorial.bearCase: Bear-market-level Nasdaq 100 drawdown, sharp Friday chip losses, broad negative breadth and elevated VIX increase risk that rallies fail. Stronger-than-expected inflation or hawkish earnings guidance could worsen the path, but are prospective scenarios.
editorial.watchNext: On Monday refresh synchronized QQQ, Nasdaq 100/Composite, SOX/SMH, VIX/VXN and breadth; check matched primary 10Y/2Y yields, CME FedWatch and same-maturity oil futures. Monitor 09:45 ET PMI, Tuesday ADI/Dell and consumer confidence, Wednesday GDP/PCE and Beige Book, and newly curated Open Watch events.
